Handspring Visor Deluxe

A Palm-style organiser sold in translucent candy colors, which the V&A links directly to the iMac G3.

Source
V&A: Visor Deluxe, W.663:1 to 8-2001
Creator
Handspring
Made
2000 (V&A); Wikipedia says the Visor line was released in September 1999
Style
Y2K aesthetic (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, techno-optimistic, shiny
Evidence
Inspected the V&A photograph of object W.663:1 to 8-2001 (image 2008BT4277, 1600 × 1200) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A says the Visor “was available in a range of translucent, coloured plastic cases, inside of which the complex computer technology is concealed. In this way, it is aesthetically related to the design of the Apple iMac G3”. The case is polypropylene. V&A W.663-2001.

Wikipedia lists the Visor Deluxe colors as translucent blue, green, and orange, and clear “Ice”, and gives a September 1999 release. Wikipedia: Handspring).

Observed

  • The case is translucent orange plastic. The circuit board and screws show through the lower part.
  • Fine horizontal ribs run down both sides of the frame around the greenish LCD screen.
  • Four round buttons and a central pill-shaped rocker are silver with a metallic sheen.
  • The device stands in a frosted, semi-clear cradle with a curved, lens-like front.
  • The stylus is a chrome tube with a white translucent tip.

Why it belongs

The Visor shows how quickly the iMac’s material language spread to small electronics: the same translucent color, now combined with small chrome parts.

The mix of warm translucent orange and cold silver is a compact version of the Y2K palette.

Borrow

Combine a translucent warm color panel with small silver pill-shaped controls.

Use a frosted clear surface as a base or stand for a colored element.
